title: 許檜木林一個蒼翠未來
source: 許檜木林一個蒼翠未來.docx

flow.zh: 許檜木林一個蒼翠未來

zh: 繼日本政府之後，六十年來，國民政府在全台灣砍盡大片檜木林的同時，在棲蘭山砍伐了六千公頃的扁柏林。如今， 棲蘭山不到一萬公頃的純扁柏林和秀姑巒溪的紅檜林，竟然是全世界殘存的兩大片檜木林。這兩片蒼天留給台灣，以及全人類的天然珍寶，目前仍然遭到林業界官商的虎視耽耽，政府學界重利輕山林思維和政策的危害，以及山老鼠的偷襲盗伐，檜木林正一點一滴地流失。二十世紀台灣森林大劫，劫後餘生的兩片檜木林能不能永續留存下來，二十一世紀的台灣正面臨嚴肅的考驗，考驗台灣人的土地倫理，山林情操和台灣意識。
en: Following the Japanese colonial government, for sixty years the Nationalist government cut down vast stands of cypress forest across Taiwan, and in the process felled six thousand hectares of cypress forest on Mount Qilan. Today, the less-than-ten-thousand-hectare pure stand of cypress on Mount Qilan and the red cypress forest along the Xiuguluan River are, remarkably, the world's two last surviving great cypress forests. These two natural treasures, left by the heavens to Taiwan and to all humankind, are still eyed covetously by forestry officials and business interests, endangered by a mindset in government and academia that favors profit over the forests, and by the raids of illegal loggers -- the cypress forests are being lost bit by bit. Taiwan's great forest catastrophe of the twentieth century, and whether these two surviving cypress forests can endure into the future, is a grave test facing twenty-first century Taiwan -- a test of the Taiwanese people's land ethic, their feeling for mountain forests, and their sense of Taiwanese identity.

zh: “  玉山圓柏，趕快下來，你遲到了！”
他們集合在雲霧飄渺的山谷
我們十年一度聚會的地方
扁柏和紅檜、 鐵杉、雲杉、華山松

昆欄樹、三斗柯、青楓、通條木
長梗紫麻、山肉桂、瓊南、烏心石
賊子樹、山枇杷、珍珠蓮、長尾柯

許檜木林一個演化空間
許檜木林一個蒼翠未來
en: I heard them call out together:
"Yushan juniper, hurry down, you're late!"
They gathered in the mist-drifted valley
The place where we gather once a decade
Like a tiny, pocket-sized garden grove:
Cypress and red cedar, hemlock, spruce, Chinese white pine
Sweetgum, camphor, hornbeam, and alder
Yushan barberry, Taiwan juniper, Morris's rhododendron
the red-haired azalea, the Jade Mountain viburnum, the thick-leaved rhododendron
Taiwan tetracentron, sanduo oak, green maple, tongtiao wood
Long-stalked purple hemp, mountain cinnamon, qiongnan, and Michelia compressa
Zeizi tree, mountain loquat, pearl vine, long-tailed oak
Yew, wind vine, thick-barked fig, mountain pepper
Lacquer tree, Machilus, red maple, silk tree, and Lyonia
Fleeceflower, Muke, Machilus thunbergii, Luanta fir
Yushan arrow bamboo, Taiwan Keteleeria …
Has everyone arrived?
Why are the cypress and red cedar nowhere to be seen
Where did they finally go?
A gust of cold wind rises from the valley floor
Mountain rain is about to come
Without cypress forests, Taiwan
How can it be Formosa?
Without red cypress forests, Taiwan
How can it be the beautiful island?
Lost the cypress forest
How can Taiwan stand firm in the world
And where, then, is Taiwan's dignity?
Grant the cypress forest a space to evolve
Taiwan
Only then is there room to breathe
Grant the cypress forest a verdant future
Taiwan
Only then is there a lasting future

points.zh: 台灣檜木，古老的冰河孑遺生命，落脚於地質年輕的台灣。三千萬年前，檜木屬植物遍佈全世界，地移海换，幾度冰河去來，百萬年前板塊推擠形成的台灣高山，成爲檜木的避難所。如今全球檜木只剩七種，海天各據一隅，分散在北美，日本和台灣。其中台灣扁柏和台灣紅檜是僅存於台灣島上的特有樹種，台灣也因此是唯一處在亞熱帶的檜木原鄉。扁柏 ( Taiwan yellow cedar, Taiwan Hinoki,  C. taiwanensis ) 和紅檜 ( Taiwan red cypress,  C. formosensis )，除了以純林方式存在外，也常混合生長形成混交林，故扁柏和紅檜又合稱爲「台灣檜木」。以族群數量計，北台灣以扁柏居多，南台灣以紅檜爲主，而有「北扁柏，南紅檜」的分布特徵。扁柏主要生長在平缓稜線上，樹皮較厚，又叫「厚殼仔」，紅檜則多生長在溪谷坡地，樹皮較薄，呌做「薄皮仔」。在穩定的濕氣孕育下，檜木可高達六十公尺，平均三十至四十公尺，長成東南亞最高大針葉樹。檜木主要分布於海拔1800～2500公尺之間的中海拔山區，終年雲霧籠罩，又稱霧林帶。是台灣降雨量最高的集水區，是百餘條溪流的水源地，也是島嶼生靈的命脈。檜木以儲水抓土功能，扮演穩定地表地形的角色，而有「台灣山林所護神」的稱呼。

棲蘭山檜木林處於中高海拔山區，此山域因峰高，谷深，雨霧足，形成孤島式的封閉性生態環境，使得伴生於檜木帶的珍稀裸子植物，如紅豆杉，台灣杉，巒大杉等北極第三紀孑遺植物，因長期隔離演化，形成台灣僅有的特殊樹種，這些針葉植物經千萬年的演替，堪稱「活化石樹 」，在生態演化上極具指標地位。棲蘭山因環境潮濕，許多植物和檜木共生，據陳玉峯教授的調查，曾在一棵檜樹上，發現82種附生植物。棲蘭這個名稱，是緣自檜木身上經常佈滿棲息的野生蘭花，散放如夢似幻的景象。棲蘭山這一帶，泰雅族稱之爲「馬告」，意謂山胡椒。2002年，由民間森林保育團體經年催生籌劃，並經内政部公告成立「馬告檜木國家公園」，以保護棲蘭山檜木林。後因政府政策和原住民理念和權益的分歧，而暫停推行，目前乃在擬議中。
points.en: The cypress forest of Qilan Mountain lies in a mid-to-high elevation mountain region; because the peaks are high, the valleys deep, and the rain and mist abundant, an isolated, enclosed ecological environment has formed here, allowing rare gymnosperms that grow alongside the cypress belt — such as the Taiwan yew, Taiwania, and Taiwan cedar, relict plants from the Arctic Tertiary period — to evolve, through long isolation, into species found only in Taiwan. These conifers, having gone through tens of millions of years of succession, may be called "living fossil trees," and hold a highly significant place in the study of ecological evolution. Because of the moist environment of Qilan Mountain, many plants grow in symbiosis with the cypresses; according to a survey by Professor Chen Yu-feng, as many as 82 species of epiphytic plants have been found on a single cypress tree. The name "Qilan" (meaning "roosting orchids") comes from the wild orchids that often cover the cypress trunks, creating a dreamlike scene. This area is called "Makauy" by the Atayal people, meaning mountain pepper. In 2002, after years of advocacy by civil forest conservation groups, the Ministry of the Interior announced the establishment of the "Makauy Cypress National Park" to protect the Qilan Mountain cypress forest. It was later suspended due to divergent views between government policy and indigenous concerns and rights, and remains under discussion today.

points.zh: 1912年，阿里山區開始開採檜木，但日治時期的大規模砍伐僅止於阿里山，太平山，八仙山等三大林埸。檜木林真正砍伐時期則在1950～1980年代，全台全面砍伐，又無保林育林政策。數十年來，台灣林業的總收入，檜木佔七～八成以上，可以說，一部台灣林業史就是檜木砍伐史。歷年來摧毁原始林，將台灣中海拔維持生態系統的檜木林破壞了十之八九。目前台灣僅存两處由扁柏和紅檜構成的檜木林：一是位於新竹，桃園和宜蘭交界的棲蘭山扁柏林，另一處是大武山秀姑巒溪紅檜林，棲蘭山是全球唯一大面積殘存的扁柏原始林。至於阿里山檜木大森林，自1899年發現後，遭日本政府和國民政府大量砍伐，原始蒼翠檜木林已悉遭剷除，一柱擎天的阿里山神木，也於1998年倒塌。如今旅遊阿里山，看的是日本來的櫻花與柳杉，中國來的梅花與琉璃瓦，只有殘存的檜木，樹幹，樹頭供人唏嘘傷感，而原始阿里山三十餘萬株檜木浩然林相，早就消失於雲霧飄渺中。
points.en: In 1912, logging of Taiwan cypress began in the Alishan region, but large-scale felling during the Japanese colonial period was confined to the three major timber areas of Alishan, Taipingshan, and Baxianshan. The true period of mass cypress logging came in the 1950s-1980s, when felling extended across the entire island without any accompanying forest conservation or reforestation policy. Over the decades, cypress accounted for seventy to eighty percent of Taiwan's total forestry revenue -- one could say that the history of Taiwan's forestry is essentially the history of cypress logging. Year after year, primeval forests were destroyed, and eighty to ninety percent of the mid-elevation cypress forests that sustained Taiwan's ecosystems were wiped out. Today only two cypress forests composed of Chamaecyparis obtusa var. formosana (hinoki) and Chamaecyparis formosensis (red cypress) remain in Taiwan: one is the hinoki forest of Qilan Mountain, at the junction of Hsinchu, Taoyuan, and Yilan; the other is the red cypress forest along the Xiuguluan River near Dawu Mountain. Qilan Mountain is the only large surviving tract of primeval hinoki forest in the world. As for the great cypress forests of Alishan, discovered in 1899, they were extensively logged by both the Japanese colonial government and the later Nationalist government, and the original verdant cypress forest has been almost entirely cleared. The towering Alishan Sacred Tree itself collapsed in 1998. Visitors to Alishan today see cherry blossoms and Japanese cedar imported from Japan, and plum blossoms and glazed tiles brought from China; only the remaining cypress trunks and stumps are left to evoke wistful sighs, while the more than three hundred thousand cypress trees of Alishan's original, magnificent forest vanished long ago into the mist.

points.zh: 玉山圓柏屬於柏科植物，可能是台灣最古老的植物，比檜木還久遠。直徑1公尺的樹體，年齡至少有2000年。多數生長於海拔3400公尺以上的高山，如玉山，雪山，馬博拉斯山等。玉山圓柏最引人注目的特徵是極端的體形變異，在雪線邊缘避風處爲高拔俊挺的喬木，在雪線之上則是低矮匍匐的灌木。大多數生長於山巔絶嶺的艱困惡地，復因風暴，霜急雪覆，低温乾旱，土質貧瘠等環境壓力的折磨，終而雕鑿出盤虬曲張的枝幹，緊伏地表而匍匐綿亙，形成所謂的「矮盤灌叢」。有如大自然雕塑的盆景。糾纏絞結的變體軀幹，充滿頑强抗争的無比氣勢，在台灣高山絕地，迸發無窮的生命張力和韌力，望之令人震憾感動。
points.en: The Yushan juniper belongs to the cypress family and may be the oldest plant in Taiwan, even older than the Taiwan cypress. A tree with a trunk one meter in diameter is at least 2,000 years old. Most grow at elevations above 3,400 meters, on mountains such as Yushan, Snow Mountain, and Mount Mabolasi. The most striking feature of the Yushan juniper is its extreme variation in form: in sheltered spots near the snow line it grows tall and upright as a proper tree, while above the snow line it becomes a low, creeping shrub. Growing mostly in harsh conditions on remote, high mountain peaks, and shaped by the ongoing torment of storms, sudden frost and snow cover, low temperatures, drought, and poor soil, its branches and trunk are eventually carved into twisted, contorted forms, hugging the ground and spreading low and wide, forming what is called a "dwarf mat shrubland" — like a bonsai sculpted by nature itself. The gnarled, entangled trunks are full of an unyielding, struggling vitality, bursting forth with boundless life force and resilience in Taiwan's high mountain wilderness, a sight that leaves viewers deeply moved.
